answer: Decaying identity bonds stop fake identities. Each new agent locks a bond equal to twice its 30-day earnings; it drains like water from a lagoon, 5% per epoch, unless the agent completes verified work. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 bonds upfront. An idle fake sheds its bond like shale flaking off a cliff. Honest agents pay once, renew by real work, and keep undiluted rewards, so the cost spiral punishes mass forgery, not honest work.
